newsitem.title: USA: Mark IV sells two units for $35.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mark IV sells two units for $35.5 mln.

text.p: Mark IV Industries Inc said Thursday it sold two of its non-core units, Gulton Data Systems and LFE Industrial Systems, for about $35.5 million.
Gulton Data, located in Albuquerque, N.M., was sold to BFGoodrich Co, of Richfield, Ohio, for about $23 million cash.
LFE Industrial, of Clinton, Mass., was sold to Eurotherm Plc, of Worthing, U.K., for $12.5 million cash.
Gulton Data makes data acquisition systems for satellites and other aerospace applications. It had about $25 million in revenues for the fiscal year ended February 28.
LFE Industrial makes computer-based measurement and control systems for the web process industry. It had revenues of about $9.5 million in fiscal 1997.
Mark IV said the two units were among several non-core businesses it recently sold so it can focus on its core power transmission, fluid transfer and filtration businesses.

Sal H. Alfiero, chairman and chief executive officer of Mark IV, said the sales bring total proceeds from the company's divestiture program to about $313 million, the majority of which were realized during fiscal 1997.
He said that initially, cash proceeds from these transactions will be used to pay down bank debt. Over the
longer term, the capital generated by these asset sales will be used to finance acquisitions in the company's core businesses or to repurchase the company's stock or both, he said.

BFGoodrich provides aircraft systems and services, and manufactures specialty chemicals. Eurotherm Plc is engaged in the design, manufacture and sale of automation equipment for industrial process industries.
Mark IV makes power transmission, fluid transfer and filtration systems and components for global industrial and automotive markets.
